name: MathVista
description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). Completing these tasks requires fine-grained, deep visual understanding and compositional reasoning.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research Redmond
citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024.
rai:dataCollection: MathVista was collected through three main approaches: (1) Collection of 9 existing math-targeted VQA datasets (GPS, MWP, TQA) with up to 400 examples per source, totaling 2,666 examples; (2) Review and collection of 19 existing general VQA datasets containing math-related instances, with automatic filtration using heuristic rules (numeric answers or quantity words) followed by manual labeling by three expert annotators using majority voting, yielding 2,739 examples; (3) Creation of three new datasets (IQTest with 228 examples, FunctionQA with 400 examples, and PaperQA with 107 examples) manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data sources include 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets. MathQA datasets include Geometry3K, GeoQA+, GEOS, UniGeo (for GPS), CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP (for MWP), and SciBench, TheoremQA (for TQA). VQA datasets include ChartQA, FigureQA, DVQA, MapQA, PlotQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA, TQA, A-OKVQA, KVQA, ParsVQA-Caps, TextVQA, VizWiz, VQA2.0, PMC-VQA, VQA-RAD, Super-CLEVR, and VQA-AS. New datasets were sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms (IQTest), functional plots (FunctionQA), and academic papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface (PaperQA).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning (examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words). The testmini subset (1,000 examples) was sampled using a two-step strategy: (1) randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset; (2) randomly sample remaining questions for each source dataset proportional to its representation in the entire set.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automatic filtration of VQA datasets yielded 4,949 examples, which were then manually labeled by three expert annotators to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. This resulted in 2,739 finalized examples. For the three new datasets, all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. Initial annotation by three reviewers achieved 99.2% inter-annotation consistency rate, with only 6 disagreements among 736 questions, which were resolved through team discussion. Several quality checks were conducted to address unidentified errors.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Examples in MathVista are annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and mathematical reasoning types. Coarse labels of mathematical reasoning were automatically obtained from source dataset details. To verify automatic annotation quality, expert annotators manually labeled mathematical reasoning categories for 1,000 examples using an annotation tool, achieving 94.1% exact match and 98.79% individual label accuracy. For the three new datasets, graduate students in STEM fields manually annotated questions, which were then reviewed through a rigorous two-step process with three independent reviewers achieving 99.2% inter-annotation consistency.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool (GUI shown in Figure 22 and Figure 23 in the paper)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement was measured using Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 for mathematical reasoning labeling, indicating substantial consistency among annotators. For the newly created datasets, initial annotation by three reviewers resulted in 99.2% inter-annotation consistency rate, with only 6 disagreements among 736 questions resolved through discussion among the entire review team.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (for manual labeling of mathematical reasoning and new dataset creation)
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields (for new dataset creation); Expert annotators with satisfactory annotating history (for mathematical reasoning labeling)
rai:machineAnnotationTools: EasyOCR (for OCR text detection), Multimodal Bard (for image caption generation)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is divided into two subsets: testmini (1,000 examples) for model development validation and test (5,141 examples) for standard evaluation. Answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination. An online evaluation platform will be maintained. The authors are committed to maintaining the datasets and refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Some examples contain images of people (e.g., celebrities for age gap questions). Multimodal Bard was restricted in responding to images of people in some cases.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts in specific domains like science and college-level math requires more labor-intensive data collection compared to textual-only or general-purpose datasets. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to heterogeneous sources. Annotations lack unified format and structure across sources. The dataset may not generalize well to other domains. Current foundation models, including GPT-4V, still fall short of human performance by 10.4%, with particular challenges in understanding complex figures, performing rigorous reasoning, logical reasoning, and numeric commonsense reasoning.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It can be used for training, testing, and validation of large language models (LLMs) and large multimodal models (LMMs). The benchmark facilitates development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios and evaluation of research progress in solving rigorous reasoning tasks. Specific use cases include figure question answering (FQA), geometry problem solving (GPS), math word problem (MWP), textbook question answering (TQA), and visual question answering (VQA).
